title: Instrumentation Coverage Audit
exclusions: Covers the detection logic documented for 'Instrumentation Coverage Audit' only. Does not supplant cross-domain SIEM playbooks for unrelated domains or regulatory attestation. Entities listed in `operational_exceptions.csv` during approved tests are excluded.
evidence: Saved search `operations_instrumentation_coverage_audit` (UC-13.5.20), SOC dashboard panel "Operations — Instrumentation Coverage Audit", and weekly export to `index=audit_evidence` sourcetype=csv:ops_controls.

controlTest.positiveScenario: UC-13.5.20 positive (Instrumentation, Coverage, Audit): ingest synthetic events into `index=traces` sourcetype='otel:traces' where `trace_count`, `operations`, `count` grouped by `service_name`, `owning_team` satisfies `count` > 0 for 'Instrumentation Coverage Audit'.  Run the saved search and confirm at least one alertable row.
controlTest.negativeScenario: UC-13.5.20 negative (Coverage Audit): ingest benign `traces` / `otel:traces` events where `service_name`, `owning_team` stays below `count` > 0, or exclude the test entity via `ops_exception_register.csv`. Variant 3 confirms zero alert rows for 'Instrumentation Coverage Audit'.

dataSources: OTel Collector receiver metrics, service registry/CMDB, `sourcetype=otel:traces` Collected via Universal Forwarder (Splunkbase 617) modular input or scripted poll into the index named in the SPL.
app: Splunk Distribution of OpenTelemetry Collector, service registry — Universal Forwarder (Splunkbase 617)
spl:
| inputlookup service_registry where status="active"
| fields service_name, owning_team, service_tier, expected_signals
| join type=left service_name [
    search index=traces sourcetype="otel:traces" earliest=-7d
    | stats dc(trace_id) as trace_count, dc(span_name) as operations by service_name
    | eval has_traces="Yes"]
| join type=left service_name [
    | mstats count(_value) as count WHERE index=otel_metrics metric_name=* BY service_name span=7d
    | where count > 0
    | eval has_metrics="Yes"
    | fields service_name, has_metrics]
| fillnull has_traces has_metrics value="No"
| eval coverage=case(
    has_traces=="Yes" AND has_metrics=="Yes", "Full",
    has_traces=="Yes" OR has_metrics=="Yes", "Partial",
    1==1, "Dark")
| stats count as total, sum(eval(if(coverage=="Full",1,0))) as full, sum(eval(if(coverage=="Partial",1,0))) as partial, sum(eval(if(coverage=="Dark",1,0))) as dark by owning_team
| eval coverage_pct=round(full*100/total, 1)
| table owning_team, total, full, partial, dark, coverage_pct
| sort coverage_pct
description: Monitors when Coverage Audit criteria fire for 'Instrumentation Coverage Audit' (UC-13.5.20) in `index=traces` sourcetype `otel:traces`. Pipeline aggregates `trace_count`, `operations`, `count` by `service_name`, `owning_team` over `7d`. Alert logic enforces `count` > 0. Title terms: Instrumentation, Coverage, Audit. Eliminates manual hunting for UC-13.5.20 conditions.
value: UC-13.5.20 helps teams contain Instrumentation, Coverage, Audit scenarios and reduce operational risk and delayed incident response before incidents compound.
implementation: Maintain a `service_registry` lookup (from CMDB, Kubernetes service discovery, or manual inventory) listing all active services with their owning team, tier, and expected telemetry signals. Compare the registry against actual telemetry received in the last 7 days: services emitting traces are "instrumented for tracing," services emitting metrics are "instrumented for metrics." Classify each service as Full (both signals), Partial (one signal), or Dark (no telemetry). Calculate coverage percentage per team. Target: 90% full coverage for Tier-1 services, 70% for Tier-2. Generate weekly instrumentation scorecards for engineering leadership. Track coverage improvement over quarters to measure observability maturity program progress.
visualization: Bar chart (coverage % by team), Table (dark services by team), Pie chart (fleet-wide coverage distribution), Line chart (coverage trend over quarters), Single value (fleet coverage %).
knownFalsePositives:
1. **Maintenance window on `traces` (UC-13.5.20)** — Planned work for 'Instrumentation Coverage Audit' shifts `trace_count`, `operations`, `count` over `span=7d` while `service_name`, `owning_team` remains in-scope.  Cross-check CMDB CHG.

2. **Batch `dc` on `otel:traces`** — Scheduled automation elevates `owning_team` without crossing `count` > 0 for UC-13.5.20. Compare `_time` minute against the job schedule.

3. **Synthetic probe on `service_name`, `owning_team`** — Health checks in `traces` populate the same fields the SPL groups on. Exclude monitoring-tagged assets before paging.

4. **Onboarding burst for `otel:traces`** — First 48h baseline for UC-13.5.20 on `service_name` is unstable; join `service_registry` prior to threshold.

**Suppression mechanism:** `ops_exception_register.csv` keyed on `service_name`, `exception_reason`, `valid_until`.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Install and configure the required add-on or app: Splunk Distribution of OpenTelemetry Collector, service registry.
• Ensure the following data sources are available: OTel Collector receiver metrics, service registry/CMDB, `sourcetype=otel:traces`.
• For app installation, inputs.conf, and Splunk directory layout, see the Implementation guide: docs/implementation-guide.md

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Maintain a `service_registry` lookup (from CMDB, Kubernetes service discovery, or manual inventory) listing all active services with their owning team, tier, and expected telemetry signals. Compare the registry against actual telemetry received in the last 7 days: services emitting traces are "instrumented for tracing," services emitting metrics are "instrumented for metrics." Classify each service as Full (both signals), Partial (one signal), or Dark (no telemetry). Calculate coverage percentag…

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
Run the following SPL in Search (then save as report or alert; adjust time range and threshold as needed):

```spl
| inputlookup service_registry where status="active"
| fields service_name, owning_team, service_tier, expected_signals
| join type=left service_name [
    search index=traces sourcetype="otel:traces" earliest=-7d
    | stats dc(trace_id) as trace_count, dc(span_name) as operations by service_name
    | eval has_traces="Yes"]
| join type=left service_name [
    | mstats count(_value) as count WHERE index=otel_metrics metric_name=* BY service_name span=7d
    | where count > 0
    | eval has_metrics="Yes"
    | fields service_name, has_metrics]
| fillnull has_traces has_metrics value="No"
| eval coverage=case(
    has_traces=="Yes" AND has_metrics=="Yes", "Full",
    has_traces=="Yes" OR has_metrics=="Yes", "Partial",
    1==1, "Dark")
| stats count as total, sum(eval(if(coverage=="Full",1,0))) as full, sum(eval(if(coverage=="Partial",1,0))) as partial, sum(eval(if(coverage=="Dark",1,0))) as dark by owning_team
| eval coverage_pct=round(full*100/total, 1)
| table owning_team, total, full, partial, dark, coverage_pct
| sort coverage_pct
```

Understanding this SPL

**Instrumentation Coverage Audit** — You can't debug what you can't see. Services without OTel instrumentation are "dark" — when they fail, you diagnose from the outside using downstream error messages and infrastructure metrics, adding 30-60 minutes to MTTR. Measuring instrumentation coverage per team (what percentage of their services emit traces, metrics, and logs with trace context) drives observability maturity programs with data rather than mandates. A coverage target of 90% for critical services creates…

Documented **Data sources**: OTel Collector receiver metrics, service registry/CMDB, `sourcetype=otel:traces`. **App/TA** (typical add-on context): Splunk Distribution of OpenTelemetry Collector, service registry. The SPL below should target the same indexes and sourcetypes you configured for that feed—rename `index=` / `sourcetype=` if your deployment differs.

**Pipeline walkthrough**

• Loads rows via `inputlookup` (KV store or CSV lookup) for enrichment or reporting.
• Keeps or drops fields with `fields` to shape columns and size.
• Joins to a subsearch with `join` — set `max=` to match cardinality and avoid silent truncation.
• Joins to a subsearch with `join` — set `max=` to match cardinality and avoid silent truncation.
• Fills null values with `fillnull`.
• `eval` defines or adjusts **coverage** — often to normalize units, derive a ratio, or prepare for thresholds.
• `stats` rolls up events into metrics; results are split **by owning_team** so each row reflects one combination of those dimensions.
• `eval` defines or adjusts **coverage_pct** — often to normalize units, derive a ratio, or prepare for thresholds.
• Pipeline stage (see **Instrumentation Coverage Audit**): table owning_team, total, full, partial, dark, coverage_pct
• Orders rows with `sort` — combine with `head`/`tail` for top-N patterns.



Step 3 — Validate
Replay with a small load change. Compare with the OTel collector logs, pipeline dashboards, and health panels for the same labels.

Step 4 — Operationalize
Add the search to a dashboard or set up alert actions (email, webhook, PagerDuty, etc.) as required. Document the use case in your runbook and assign an owner.
